annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and exact first-order product-expansion formalization

assumptions: P is a finite sequence of exact square transformations and E is the corresponding sequence of local perturbations.
The scalar t marks every occurrence of a local perturbation.
No orthogonality assumption is needed for this purely algebraic expansion; the paper uses it only in the subsequent norm estimates.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P06 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P06 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p06_t3_householder_product_first_order_expansion {m : Nat} (t : Real) (P E : Nat -> Fin m -> Fin m -> Real) (b : Fin m -> Real) : forall r i, perturbedState r i = exactState r i + t * firstOrderState r i + t^2 * higherOrderState r i
formal_statement.plain_language: A product of transformations P_j+tE_j is exactly its unperturbed state plus t times all single-error insertions plus t squared times an explicit higher-order remainder.

informal_proof: Induct on the sequence length. Distribute the newest factor P_r+tE_r over the induction hypothesis, collect the terms with zero and one E factors, and identify the remaining terms with the recursive higher-order state.
informal_statement: An exact finite version of the first-order product expansion and O(u^2) remainder in equations (4.8)-(4.9).
